summary: Backend-only test of Shipment Labels (Phase F4.1). Executed 23 pytest cases across A (CRUD), B (shipment assignment), C (delete cleanup), D (regression), E (multi-user isolation). Result: 22 PASSED, 1 FAILED. All Labels router endpoints work correctly at the API+DB layer. However, GET /api/shipments STRIPS the newly-added `labels` field on every response because the Pydantic `Shipment` model in server.py does not declare it — so clients can never see the labels a shipment was assigned. PUT /api/shipments/{id}/labels returns 200 with correct labels in the response, and DB write is correct (verified in test C3 cleanup succeeded), but the round-trip through GET is broken.

critical.issue: The `labels: string[]` field added to shipment docs by PUT /api/shipments/{id}/labels is stripped on every GET because the Pydantic Shipment model in /app/backend/server.py (lines ~562-666) has no `labels` field. Pydantic drops unknown fields, so clients always see `labels: undefined/None`. Fix: add `labels: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)` to the Shipment model. This breaks spec item D1 (`optional labels: string[] field on each row`) and blocks the frontend chip UI from displaying assigned labels after a reload.

action_items: Add `labels: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)` to the Pydantic `Shipment` model in /app/backend/server.py so GET /api/shipments and GET /api/shipments/{id} include the assigned labels. This is the single fix required — the labels router itself is correct.

(Optional, but useful for symmetry) Add `labels: Optional[List[str]] = None` to the `ShipmentUpdate` model too if PUT /api/shipments/{id} should also accept labels changes; for F4.1 the dedicated /api/shipments/{id}/labels endpoint is enough.
After the fix, re-run `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_shipment_labels_phase_f41.py -v` — all 23 tests should pass.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/labels.py is clean, well-documented, and defensive (case-insensitive dedupe, silent-drop of invalid ids, 20-label cap, delete cleanup via $pull, user-scoped queries throughout). No _id leakage.

The mismatch between the labels router (writes `labels` to shipment doc) and the Shipment Pydantic model (has no `labels` field, therefore reads strip it) is the only integration gap and is exactly the kind of thing that hurts feature-scope split across two files. Suggest keeping a comment on the Shipment model pointing at labels.py so future maintainers don't drop the field again.

rca_of_issue: Bug: GET /api/shipments never returns the newly-added `labels` array even though PUT /api/shipments/{id}/labels writes it to Mongo correctly. Reproduction: (1) POST /api/auth/login as admin; (2) PUT /api/shipments/<sid>/labels with {labels:[<real_id_1>,<real_id_2>]} → response is 200 {ok:true, labels:[<id1>,<id2>]}; (3) GET /api/shipments?limit=1 → the shipment doc has NO `labels` key. Cause: /app/backend/routers/shipments_read.py returns `Shipment(**doc)` (Pydantic model). The Shipment model in server.py doesn't declare a `labels` field, so Pydantic silently strips it. Mitigation: Add `labels: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)` to the Shipment model. Single-line fix, no other code changes needed.
